title: Rust TreeCore (v0.5.19) shows e2e regression at concurrency on small dense model
body:
## Summary

The Rust TreeCore backend (`SGLANG_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE_CORE_BACKEND=rust`), shipped as opt-in in v0.5.19, shows a measurable end-to-end regression at concurrency compared to the Python TreeCore backend, on a small dense model with a short shared prefix workload. The PR (#32710) notes end-to-end benchmarking as a "planned follow-up" — this is an independent data point for that.

## Setup

- **Model**: Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct (dense, bf16)
- **GPU**: RTX 4090 (single GPU, TP=1)
- **Engine**: SGLang v0.5.19 (`lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.19` Docker image)
- **Workload**: streaming tool-call completions with the stock `qwen` tool parser, 2 tool calls per request, 10.2–10.4 deltas/request (identical across all arms — no granularity confound)
- **Shared prefix**: system prompt + tool JSON schema, order hundreds of tokens (not 61K-token class like the C++ PR's benchmark)
- **Concurrency**: 8, 64, 256 concurrent requests; 3 rounds per level, medians reported

## Three-arm A/B

Three arms, same image, same model, same GPU:

| arm | version | TreeCore backend |
|---|---|---|
| `stock` | v0.5.18 | plain RadixCache (no unified tree) |
| `python` | v0.5.19 | Python TreeCore (unified, default) |
| `rust` | v0.5.19 | Rust TreeCore (`SGLANG_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE_CORE_BACKEND=rust`) |

Baseline for comparison: `python` arm (same version, isolating only the TreeCore backend).

## Results (median of 3 rounds)

| conc | metric | python (0.5.19) | rust (0.5.19) | delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8 | stream_span | 189.6 ms | 189.6 ms | −0.0% |
| 8 | e2e p50 | 278 ms | 275 ms | −0.9% |
| 8 | CPU | 172% | 161% | −6% |
| 64 | stream_span | 367.4 ms | 395.3 ms | **+7.6%** |
| 64 | e2e p50 | 606 ms | 678 ms | **+11.9%** |
| 64 | TTFT p50 | 223.7 ms | 249.9 ms | +11.7% |
| 64 | ITL p50 | 11.0 ms | 12.5 ms | +14.2% |
| 64 | CPU | 172% | 161% | −6% |
| 256 | stream_span | 515.9 ms | 562.6 ms | **+9.1%** |
| 256 | e2e p50 | 1208 ms | 1340 ms | **+10.9%** |
| 256 | TTFT p50 | 664.2 ms | 752.2 ms | +13.2% |
| 256 | ITL p50 | 24.8 ms | 24.3 ms | −1.8% |
| 256 | CPU | 172% | 161% | −6% |

`stream_span` is a delta-count-invariant metric (total streaming wall time / number of deltas), so it is not confounded by arms emitting different chunk counts. Delta counts were identical across all arms at every concurrency level.

IQRs at conc 64: stream_span python IQR 19.8 ms, rust IQR 19.1 ms, against a 28 ms difference. IQRs at conc 256: python IQR 30.2 ms, rust IQR 29.9 ms, against a 47 ms difference. The gap is larger than the spread at both levels.

## Observations

1. **The Rust backend is slower at concurrency, not faster.** At conc 8 the arms are identical. At conc 64 and 256, `stream_span`, e2e, and TTFT all regress by 8–13%.

2. **Rust uses ~6% less CPU while being slower.** This points at blocking/overhead (PyO3 boundary crossings, GIL round-trips, or lock contention) rather than the tree algorithm itself being computationally slow — the CPU savings should have produced a speedup, not a regression.

3. **The engine-version control is clean.** stock (0.5.18, plain RadixCache) vs python (0.5.19, Python TreeCore) on `stream_span`: +0.1% / −0.0% / −0.4% at conc 8/64/256. The 0.5.18→0.5.19 upgrade, including the switch to the unified cache class, is a no-op for this workload, so the python-vs-rust difference is purely the TreeCore backend.

## Limitation

Our workload has a short shared prefix (system prompt + tool schema, order hundreds of tokens), not the 61K-token shared prefix used in the C++ radix tree PR (#36128). So this round measures the Rust backend's **overhead** when the cache is not under pressure, and does not test whether the backend pays off under prefix-heavy load. A prefix-heavy workload would be needed to claim the latter — but that regime was already tested end-to-end by the C++ PR and found flat.

## Repro

```bash
docker pull lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.19
docker pull lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.18

# Start server with Rust TreeCore backend
docker run --rm --gpus all -p 8000:8000 -v $HOME/hf-cache:/hf -e HF_HOME=/hf \
  -e SGLANG_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE_CORE_BACKEND=rust \
  lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.19 \
  python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct \
  --port 8000 --host 0.0.0.0 --context-length 4096 --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \
  --tool-call-parser qwen

# Start server with Python TreeCore backend (control)
# Same command, but: -e SGLANG_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE_CORE_BACKEND=python
```

Workload: streaming chat completions with tool calls, 2 calls per request, at concurrency 8/64/256. Full A/B harness and raw results: [infe/bench/results/rtx4090-20260908-round6/](https://github.com/sejori/infe/tree/main/bench/results/rtx4090-20260908-round6).

Happy to run a prefix-heavy variant if that would help disambiguate overhead from benefit.
